rendered: NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated within a pH window of about 10[1] to 12[2]. The reason is that the metals precipitate at different pH values. Hydroxides of aluminum start precipitating at a lower pH than hydroxides of nickel and iron, which precipitate only beyond pH 6[3]. Simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron and aluminum is therefore difficult because of the varying solubility product (Ksp) of the hydroxide precipitates, and the window is narrowed to the range shown above.[4] To make the precursors, the outflow from the reactor is filtered, washed and dried to obtain the hydroxide precursors.[5] The dried hydroxides are then mixed with a lithium source (Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.)[6] and calcined in an O2-rich environment at temperatures above >600 °C[7]. The resulting NFA cathode powder is then cast into electrodes by a roll-to-roll slot-die coating process and assembled into cobalt-free pouch cells.[8]
